title: New Frontiers of India-France Relations
description: This editorial is based on “Technology drives India-France strategic convergence” published in The Hindu on 16/06/2026. The article emphasizes the evolving Special Global Strategic Partnership, highlighting how innovation, digital cooperation, and joint technological research are replacing traditional security-centric ties as the core pillars of the deepening India-France bilateral relationship. For Prelims: Global South, Multi-Role Fighter Aircraft (MRFA), Varuna, Shakti, Garuda, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Quantum Computing, TRISHNA Mission, International Solar Alliance (ISA), Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI), Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), European Union, Green Hydrogen, UPI, IMF, World Bank, Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, GDPR, SHANTI Act, 2026, Convention on Supplementary Compensation for Nuclear Damage (CSC), Section 3(d) of the Patents Act, 1970, Dark Vessels, Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) For Mains: Key areas of convergence and divergence between India and France, Measures needed to deepen the India–France strategic partnership. India and France are accelerating their strategic partnership by prioritizing technology, innovation, and co-production under the "Horizon 2047" framework. Despite geopolitical and regulatory divergences, both nations are leveraging their status as middle powers to ensure stability. This collaboration increasingly emphasizes resilient supply chains and climate-centric development for the Global South.

title: National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA): India’s Drug Price Regulator
description: Subject: Polity & Governance / Health Sector Governance / Economy (Drug Price Regulation, National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM), Drug Price Control Order (DPCO), Pharmaceutical Sector) Why in News? The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) recently increased the ceiling prices of two critical anti-cancer drugs—Cisplatin and Carboplatin—by 50% to address shortages caused by rising platinum prices and supply-chain disruptions. The decision was taken under special public-interest provisions to ensure uninterrupted availability of these life-saving medicines. title: Equality of Treatment for Persons with Disabilities
description: GS Paper II – Social Justice (Social Security) | GS Paper I – Society | GS Paper IV – Ethics Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016; Disability Pension; Article 41; Dignity; Inclusive Welfare Despite India’s emergence as a digital welfare state, Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) remain excluded due to uneven pension policies, bureaucratic hurdles, and low public spending. India spends only 0.02% of GDP on disability welfare, far below countries like Brazil and South Africa, leaving many PwDs outside the reach of inclusive social security. India’s Spending on Disability Welfare (including pensions): GDP Loss Due to Exclusion (World Bank & UNDP): The Proposal: Minimum Universal Disability Pension Floor Rate (MUDPFR) Comparison with Other Expenditures (fiscally manageable): Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016: Institutional Reform: Need for a Single National Authority Combining Pensions with Employment Support India’s Existing Schemes (Foundation for Expansion): Constitutional Imperative and Moral Argument India spends only 0.02% of GDP on disability welfare despite evidence that excluding PwDs causes major economic losses. A proposed universal disability pension of ₹8,000 per month would cost just 0.08% of GDP and is fiscally feasible. Backed by Article 41, the RPwD Act, and global models like South Africa and Brazil, India needs a uniform national disability pension system to ensure dignity and inclusive welfare for all PwDs. https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/lead/equality-of-treatment-for-persons-with-disabilities/article71094672.ece
